sanskrit: ity evaṃ dharmataḥ khyātam ṛṣibhir dharmavādibhiḥ pumān yajñaś ca somaś ca nyāyavṛtto yathā bhavet anyāyavṛttaḥ puruṣo na parasya na cātmanaḥ
english: Thus has it been proclaimed in accordance with dharma by the seers who expound the dharma: the man, and the sacrifice, and the Soma should all be conducted by lawful means; for the man who proceeds by unlawful means is of no use to another, nor even to himself.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ yajñapātrāṇi ity eṣā śrūyate śrutiḥ tāni samyak praṇītāni brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām
english: "The body is the vessel of the sacrifice" — so runs this scriptural saying; and in the case of great-souled brāhmaṇas these vessels are rightly consecrated.

sanskrit: tapo yajñād api śreṣṭham ity eṣā paramā śrutiḥ tat te tapaḥ pravakṣyāmi vidvaṃs tad api me śṛṇu
english: "Austerity is higher even than sacrifice" — this is the supreme scriptural truth. I shall now declare that austerity to you, O learned one; hear it from me as well.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyavacanam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ damo ghṛṇā etat tapo vidur dhīrā na śarīrasya śoṣaṇam
english: Non-injury, truthful speech, freedom from cruelty, self-restraint, and compassion — this the wise know to be austerity, and not the wasting away of the body.

sanskrit: aprāmāṇyaṃ ca vedānāṃ śāstrāṇāṃ cātilaṅghanam avyavasthā ca sarvatra tad vai nāśanam ātmanaḥ
english: To deny the authority of the Vedas, to transgress the scriptures, and to live everywhere without rule and order — that, indeed, is the ruin of the self.

sanskrit: nibodha daśahotṝṇāṃ vidhānaṃ pārtha yādṛśam cittiḥ sruk cittam ājyaṃ ca pavitraṃ jñānam uttamam
english: Learn, O Pārtha, the nature of the ordinance of the ten priests of inward sacrifice: understanding is the ladle, the mind is the clarified butter, and supreme knowledge is the purifying strainer.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ jihmaṃ mṛtyupadam ārjavaṃ brahmaṇaḥ padam etāvāñ jñānaviṣayaḥ kiṃ pralāpaḥ kariṣyati
english: All that is crooked is the road to death; uprightness is the road to Brahman. Such is the whole scope of knowledge — what will idle babbling accomplish?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad apy alpataraṃ karma tad apy ekena duṣkaram puruṣeṇāsahāyena kim u rājyaṃ pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Even a slighter task is hard for a single man to accomplish without a helper — how much more, then, the rule of a kingdom, O grandsire?

sanskrit: kiṃśīlaḥ kiṃsamācāro rājño 'rthasacivo bhavet kīdṛśe viśvased rājā kīdṛśe nāpi viśvaset
english: Of what character and what conduct should a king's minister of affairs be? In what sort of man should a king place his trust, and in what sort should he place none?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca caturvidhāni mitrāṇi rājñāṃ rājan bhavanty uta sahārtho bhajamānaś ca sahajaḥ kṛtrimas tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: Kings, O king, have friends of four kinds: the ally bound by a shared interest, the loyal partisan, the friend by birth, and the friend made by contrivance.

sanskrit: dharmātmā pañcamaṃ mitraṃ sa tu naikasya na dvayoḥ yato dharmas tato vā syān madhyastho vā tato bhavet
english: The righteous-souled man is a fifth kind of friend; but he belongs neither to one party nor to two — he stands on whichever side dharma stands, or else he remains neutral.

sanskrit: yas tasyārtho na roceta na taṃ tasya prakāśayet dharmādharmeṇa rājānaś caranti vijigīṣavaḥ
english: Whatever design of his own may not please that righteous one, the king should not disclose to him; for kings bent on conquest move now by right means and now by wrong.

sanskrit: caturṇāṃ madhyamau śreṣṭhau nityaṃ śaṅkyau tathāparau sarve nityaṃ śaṅkitavyāḥ pratyakṣaṃ kāryam ātmanaḥ
english: Of the four, the two middle kinds are the best; the other two are ever to be suspected. Indeed all are ever to be watched with caution, and the king's own business must be seen to before his very eyes.

sanskrit: na hi rājñā pramādo vai kartavyo mitrarakṣaṇe pramādinaṃ hi rājānaṃ lokāḥ paribhavanty uta
english: For the king must never be negligent in the safeguarding of his friends; a negligent king the people surely come to despise.

sanskrit: asādhuḥ sādhutām eti sādhur bhavati dāruṇaḥ ariś ca mitraṃ bhavati mitraṃ cāpi praduṣyati
english: The bad man turns to goodness, the good man becomes harsh; the foe becomes a friend, and the friend in turn grows corrupt.

sanskrit: anityacittaḥ puruṣas tasmin ko jātu viśvaset tasmāt pradhānaṃ yat kāryaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tat samācaret
english: A man's mind is ever changeable — who could ever wholly trust him? Therefore whatever business is of chief importance, that the king should carry out under his own eye.

sanskrit: ekāntena hi viśvāsaḥ kṛtsno dharmārthanāśakaḥ aviśvāsaś ca sarvatra mṛtyunā na viśiṣyate
english: Trust placed wholly and without reserve is the destroyer of both dharma and material gain; yet distrust of everyone everywhere is no better than death itself.

sanskrit: akālamṛtyur viśvāso viśvasan hi vipadyate yasmin karoti viśvāsam icchatas tasya jīvati
english: Trust is an untimely death, for he who trusts comes to ruin; he survives only at the pleasure of the man in whom he has placed his trust.

sanskrit: tasmād viśvasitavyaṃ ca śaṅkitavyaṃ ca keṣu cit eṣā nītigatis tāta lakṣmīś caiva sanātanī
english: Therefore in some men one should trust, and in some one should be wary — this is the course of statecraft, my child, and the everlasting way of Fortune herself.

sanskrit: yaṃ manyeta mamābhāvād imam arthāgamaḥ spṛśet nityaṃ tasmāc chaṅkitavyam amitraṃ taṃ vidur budhāḥ
english: The man of whom one thinks, "By my downfall this gain would come to him" — of him one must ever be wary; the wise know such a one to be an enemy.

sanskrit: yasya kṣetrād apy udakaṃ kṣetram anyasya gacchati na tatrānicchatas tasya bhidyeran sarvasetavaḥ
english: From whose field the water flows down into another's field — there, against his will, all his dykes are liable to be broken through.

sanskrit: tathaivāty udakād bhītas tasya bhedanam icchati yam evaṃlakṣaṇaṃ vidyāt tam amitraṃ vinirdiśet
english: And so too the man below, afraid of the excess of water, wishes to break those dykes; whomever one perceives to bear such a mark, him one should mark out as a foe.

sanskrit: yaḥ samṛddhyā na tuṣyeta kṣaye dīnataro bhavet etad uttamamitrasya nimittam abhicakṣate
english: He who is not gladdened by your prosperity, and who grows more wretched at your decline — this they declare to be the sign of the highest friend.

sanskrit: yaṃ manyeta mamābhāvād asyābhāvo bhaved iti tasmin kurvīta viśvāsaṃ yathā pitari vai tathā
english: The man of whom one thinks, "By my downfall his own downfall would follow" — in him one should place trust, even as one would in a father.

sanskrit: taṃ śaktyā vardhamānaś ca sarvataḥ paribṛṃhayet nityaṃ kṣatād vārayati yo dharmeṣv api karmasu
english: Him, as one prospers, one should foster to the utmost by every means — the friend who ever guards one from harm, both in matters of dharma and in one's undertakings.

sanskrit: kṣatād bhītaṃ vijānīyād uttamaṃ mitralakṣaṇam ye tasya kṣatam icchanti te tasya ripavaḥ smṛtāḥ
english: One should know fear of one's harm to be the highest mark of a friend; those who desire one's harm are reckoned one's enemies.

sanskrit: vyasanān nityabhīto 'sau samṛddhyām eva tṛpyate yat syād evaṃvidhaṃ mitraṃ tad ātmasamam ucyate
english: He who is ever fearful of one's misfortune and contented only in one's prosperity — such a friend, when one is found, is said to be as one's own self.

sanskrit: rūpavarṇasvaropetas titikṣur anasūyakaḥ kulīnaḥ śīlasaṃpannaḥ sa te syāt pratyanantaraḥ
english: Endowed with fair form, complexion, and bearing, patient and free from envy, well-born and rich in good character — such a man may be your nearest confidant.

sanskrit: medhāvī smṛtimān dakṣaḥ prakṛtyā cānṛśaṃsavān yo mānito 'mānito vā na saṃdūṣyet kadā cana
english: Intelligent, of good memory, capable, and by nature free from cruelty, one who, whether honored or unhonored, would never turn malicious — such a man is fit.

sanskrit: ṛtvig vā yadi vācāryaḥ sakhā vātyantasaṃstutaḥ gṛhe vased amātyas te yaḥ syāt paramapūjitaḥ
english: Be he a priest, or a preceptor, or a comrade greatly esteemed — such a minister should dwell in your house, one who is held in the highest honor.

sanskrit: sa te vidyāt paraṃ mantraṃ prakṛtiṃ cārthadharmayoḥ viśvāsas te bhavet tatra yathā pitari vai tathā
english: He may know your most secret counsel and the very ground of your interests and your dharma; in him your trust may rest, even as it would in a father.

sanskrit: naiva dvau na trayaḥ kāryā na mṛṣyeran parasparam ekārthād eva bhūtānāṃ bhedo bhavati sarvadā
english: Neither two nor three such should be appointed, lest they fail to bear with one another; for it is from a single shared interest that strife among beings ever arises.

sanskrit: kīrtipradhāno yaś ca syād yaś ca syāt samaye sthitaḥ samarthān yaś ca na dveṣṭi samarthān kurute ca yaḥ
english: He who holds fame above all, who stands firm to his agreement, who does not hate the able but rather makes men able —

sanskrit: yo na kāmād bhayāl lobhāt krodhād vā dharmam utsṛjet dakṣaḥ paryāptavacanaḥ sa te syāt pratyanantaraḥ
english: who would not abandon dharma out of desire, fear, greed, or anger, and who is capable and weighty in his counsel — such a man may be your nearest confidant.

sanskrit: śūraś cāryaś ca vidvāṃś ca pratipattiviśāradaḥ kulīnaḥ śīlasaṃpannas titikṣur anasūyakaḥ
english: Brave and noble, learned and skilled in resolve, well-born and of upright character, patient and free from envy —

sanskrit: ete hy amātyāḥ kartavyāḥ sarvakarmasv avasthitāḥ pūjitāḥ saṃvibhaktāś ca susahāyāḥ svanuṣṭhitāḥ
english: these are the men to be made ministers, set over all affairs, honored and given their due share, well-supported and well-established.

sanskrit: kṛtsnam ete vinikṣiptāḥ pratirūpeṣu karmasu yuktā mahatsu kāryeṣu śreyāṃsy utpādayanti ca
english: When such men are wholly assigned to the tasks that befit them, and set to weighty undertakings, they bring forth the greatest goods.

sanskrit: ete karmāṇi kurvanti spardhamānā mithaḥ sadā anutiṣṭhanti caivārthān ācakṣāṇāḥ parasparam
english: These men perform their tasks, ever vying with one another, and they accomplish their objects, reporting them each to each.

sanskrit: jñātibhyaś caiva bibhyethā mṛtyor iva yataḥ sadā uparājeva rājardhiṃ jñātir na sahate sadā
english: And of your kinsmen you should be ever afraid, as of death itself; for as a rival king cannot endure a king's prosperity, so a kinsman never can.

sanskrit: ṛjor mṛdor vadānyasya hrīmataḥ satyavādinaḥ nānyo jñāter mahābāho vināśam abhinandati
english: Of the upright, the gentle, the generous, the modest, the truthful man — none, O mighty-armed one, rejoices in his ruin so much as a kinsman.

sanskrit: ajñātitā nātisukhā nāvajñeyās tv ataḥ param ajñātimantaṃ puruṣaṃ pare paribhavanty uta
english: Yet to be without kinsmen is no great happiness either; and beyond that they are not to be despised, for the man who has no kinsmen, strangers indeed hold in contempt.

sanskrit: nikṛtasya narair anyair jñātir eva parāyaṇam nānyair nikāraṃ sahate jñāter jñātiḥ kadā cana
english: For the man wronged by others, his kinsman alone is his refuge; never does one kinsman endure to see another humiliated by outsiders.

sanskrit: ātmānam eva jānāti nikṛtaṃ bāndhavair api teṣu santi guṇāś caiva nairguṇyaṃ teṣu lakṣyate
english: Even when wronged by his own kin, a man knows it as a wound to himself; in them there are virtues, and in them too defects are seen.

sanskrit: nājñātir anugṛhṇāti nājñātir digdham asyati ubhayaṃ jñātilokeṣu dṛśyate sādhv asādhu ca
english: One who is no kinsman neither shows favor nor hurls the poisoned shaft; but in the world of kinsmen both are seen — the good and the bad alike.

sanskrit: tān mānayet pūjayec ca nityaṃ vācā ca karmaṇā kuryāc ca priyam etebhyo nāpriyaṃ kiṃ cid ācaret
english: Them one should honor and ever revere, in word and in deed, and do what is pleasing to them, and never do anything displeasing.

sanskrit: viśvastavad aviśvastas teṣu varteta sarvadā na hi doṣo guṇo veti nispṛktas teṣu dṛśyate
english: Toward them one should always conduct oneself as though trusting, yet untrusting; for there is no man free of fault or of virtue to be found among them.

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya puruṣasyāpramādinaḥ amitrāḥ saṃprasīdanti tathā mitrībhavanty api
english: For the man who conducts himself thus and is never negligent, even his enemies grow well-disposed, and they too become his friends.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vartate nityaṃ jñātisaṃbandhimaṇḍale mitreṣv amitreṣv aiśvarye ciraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati
english: He who ever conducts himself thus, within the circle of his kinsmen and connections, among friends and foes alike, abides long in sovereignty and in glory.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evam agrāhyake tasmiñ jñātisaṃbandhimaṇḍale mitreṣv amitreṣv api ca kathaṃ bhāvo vibhāvyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When that circle of kinsmen and connections is thus not to be grasped, how is one's true disposition to be made plain, among friends and foes alike?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam vāsudevasya saṃvādaṃ surarṣer nāradasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount an ancient tale — the dialogue of Vāsudeva and the divine sage Nārada.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca nāsuhṛt paramaṃ mantraṃ nāradārhati veditum apaṇḍito vāpi suhṛt paṇḍito vāpi nātmavān
english: Vāsudeva said: One who is no true friend does not deserve to know one's deepest counsel, O Nārada, nor does a friend who is foolish, nor even a wise man who lacks self-command.

sanskrit: sa te sauhṛdam āsthāya kiṃ cid vakṣyāmi nārada kṛtsnāṃ ca buddhiṃ saṃprekṣya saṃpṛcche tridivaṃgama
english: Relying upon your friendship, I shall tell you something, O Nārada; and beholding the whole of your understanding, I ask of you, O traveler of the triple heaven.

sanskrit: dāsyam aiśvaryavādena jñātīnāṃ vai karomy aham ardhabhoktāsmi bhogānāṃ vāgduruktāni ca kṣame
english: I render service to my kinsmen under the mere name of lordship; I am but a half-sharer in enjoyments, and I bear with their harsh words besides.

sanskrit: araṇīm agnikāmo vā mathnāti hṛdayaṃ mama vācā duruktaṃ devarṣe tan me dahati nityadā
english: As one desiring fire churns the fire-stick, so do their harsh words churn my heart; that ill-spoken speech, O divine sage, burns me without end.

sanskrit: balaṃ saṃkarṣaṇe nityaṃ saukumāryaṃ punar gade rūpeṇa mattaḥ pradyumnaḥ so 'sahāyo 'smi nārada
english: Strength dwells ever in Saṃkarṣaṇa, and softness again in Gada; Pradyumna is intoxicated with his own beauty — and so I am without a helper, O Nārada.

sanskrit: anye hi sumahābhāgā balavanto durāsadāḥ nityotthānena saṃpannā nāradāndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ
english: And the other Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, O Nārada, are men of great fortune, mighty and hard to assail, and endowed with unceasing energy.

sanskrit: yasya na syur na vai sa syād yasya syuḥ kṛcchram eva tat dvābhyāṃ nivārito nityaṃ vṛṇomy ekataraṃ na ca
english: He who lacks them would be as nothing; yet for him who has them it is sheer distress. Held back forever between two factions, I cannot choose either one.

sanskrit: syātāṃ yasyāhukākrūrau kiṃ nu duḥkhataraṃ tataḥ yasya vāpi na tau syātāṃ kiṃ nu duḥkhataraṃ tataḥ
english: For him who has both Āhuka and Akrūra, what could be more grievous than that? And for him who has neither of those two, what could be more grievous than that?

sanskrit: so 'haṃ kitavamāteva dvayor api mahāmune ekasya jayam āśaṃse dvitīyasyāparājayam
english: I am like the mother of two gamblers, O great sage: for the one I wish victory, and for the other no defeat.

sanskrit: mamaivaṃ kliśyamānasya nāradobhayataḥ sadā vaktum arhasi yac chreyo jñātīnām ātmanas tathā
english: As I am thus ever afflicted on both sides, O Nārada, you ought to tell me what is best, both for my kinsmen and for myself.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca āpado dvividhāḥ kṛṣṇa bāhyāś cābhyantarāś ca ha prādurbhavanti vārṣṇeya svakṛtā yadi vānyataḥ
english: Nārada said: Calamities are of two kinds, O Kṛṣṇa — outer and inner, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis — and they arise whether self-wrought or sprung from another.

sanskrit: seyam ābhyantarā tubhyam āpat kṛcchrā svakarmajā akrūrabhojaprabhavāḥ sarve hy ete tadanvayāḥ
english: This grievous calamity of yours is the inner kind, born of your own deeds; for all these troubles spring from Akrūra and the Bhojas and follow in their train.

sanskrit: arthahetor hi kāmād vādvārā bībhatsayāpi vā ātmanā prāptam aiśvaryam anyatra pratipāditam
english: For the sake of gain, or out of desire, or through Dvāravatī, or even from loathing, the sovereignty you yourself had won was made over to others.

sanskrit: kṛtamūlam idānīṃ taj jātaśabdaṃ sahāyavat na śakyaṃ punar ādātuṃ vāntam annam iva tvayā
english: Now that lordship has struck root, has gained renown, and has won its supporters; it cannot be taken back again by you, any more than food once vomited up.

sanskrit: babhrūgrasenayo rājyaṃ nāptuṃ śakyaṃ kathaṃ cana jñātibhedabhayāt kṛṣṇa tvayā cāpi viśeṣataḥ
english: The kingdom of Babhru and Ugrasena can in no way be regained — out of fear of a split among the kinsmen, O Kṛṣṇa, and least of all by you.

sanskrit: tac cet sidhyet prayatnena kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram mahākṣayavyayaṃ vā syād vināśo vā punar bhavet
english: And if it should be accomplished by great effort, after performing a most arduous deed, it would bring vast ruin and expense, or else destruction would come once again.

sanskrit: anāyasena śastreṇa mṛdunā hṛdayacchidā jihvām uddhara sarveṣāṃ parimṛjyānumṛjya ca
english: With a weapon not of iron, soft, yet cleaving to the very heart, draw out the tongue of all of them, stroking and soothing them again and again.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca anāyasaṃ mune śastraṃ mṛdu vidyām ahaṃ katham yenaiṣām uddhare jihvāṃ parimṛjyānumṛjya ca
english: Vāsudeva said: How, O sage, am I to know that weapon — not of iron, and soft — by which I may draw out their tongue, stroking and soothing them again and again?

sanskrit: nārada uvāca śaktyānnadānaṃ satataṃ titikṣā dama ārjavam yathārhapratipūjā ca śastram etad anāyasam
english: Nārada said: The constant giving of food to the best of one's power, forbearance, self-restraint, uprightness, and honoring each according to his due — this is the weapon not of iron.

sanskrit: jñātīnāṃ vaktukāmānāṃ kaṭūni ca laghūni ca girā tvaṃ hṛdayaṃ vācaṃ śamayasva manāṃsi ca
english: When your kinsmen are minded to speak words bitter and slighting, do you with gentle speech quiet their hearts, their words, and their minds.

sanskrit: nāmahāpuruṣaḥ kaś cin nānātmā nāsahāyavān mahatīṃ dhuram ādatte tām udyamyorasā vaha
english: No one who is not a great man, none lacking self-command, none without helpers, takes up the mighty yoke; lift it up and bear it upon your breast.

sanskrit: sarva eva guruṃ bhāram anaḍvān vahate same durge pratīkaḥ sugavo bhāraṃ vahati durvaham
english: Any ox at all bears a heavy load on level ground; but on rough roads it is the well-made, sturdy bullock that bears the burden hard to carry.

sanskrit: bhedād vināśaḥ saṃghānāṃ saṃghamukhyo 'si keśava yathā tvāṃ prāpya notsīded ayaṃ saṃghas tathā kuru
english: From division comes the ruin of confederacies; you are the chief of your confederacy, O Keśava. So act that this confederacy, having you, may not be brought to ruin.

sanskrit: nānyatra buddhikṣāntibhyāṃ nānyatrendriyanigrahāt nānyatra dhanasaṃtyāgād gaṇaḥ prājñe 'vatiṣṭhate
english: By nothing but wisdom and patience, by nothing but mastery of the senses, by nothing but the giving up of wealth, does a community hold together in a wise leader.

sanskrit: dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ svapakṣodbhāvanaṃ śubham jñātīnām avināśaḥ syād yathā kṛṣṇa tathā kuru
english: So act, O Kṛṣṇa, that the destruction of your kinsmen may be averted — a thing fortunate, glorious, life-giving, and auspicious, which exalts your own party.

sanskrit: āyatyāṃ ca tadātve ca na te 'sty aviditaṃ prabho ṣāḍguṇyasya vidhānena yātrāyānavidhau tathā
english: For the future and for the present alike, nothing is unknown to you, O lord — neither the ordering of the six measures of policy, nor the manner of march and of march against the foe.

sanskrit: mādhavāḥ kukurā bhojāḥ sarve cāndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ tvayy āsaktā mahābāho lokā lokeśvarāś ca ye
english: The Mādhavas, the Kukuras, the Bhojas, and all the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis depend upon you, O mighty-armed one — yes, and the worlds too, and those who are lords of the worlds.

sanskrit: upāsate hi tvadbuddhim ṛṣayaś cāpi mādhava tvaṃ guruḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ jānīṣe tvaṃ gatāgatam tvām āsādya yaduśreṣṭham edhante jñātinaḥ sukham
english: The seers too wait upon your wisdom, O Mādhava; you are the teacher of all beings, you know the going and the coming of all things; and having you, O best of the Yadus, your kinsmen thrive in happiness.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca eṣā prathamato vṛttir dvitīyāṃ śṛṇu bhārata yaḥ kaś cij janayed arthaṃ rājñā rakṣyaḥ sa mānavaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: This is the first mode of conduct; now hear the second, O Bhārata. Whatsoever man brings forth wealth for the king, that man the king should protect.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇam amātyena bhṛto vā yadi vābhṛtaḥ yo rājakośaṃ naśyantam ācakṣīta yudhiṣṭhira
english: Whoever — whether in the king's pay or not — should report that the royal treasury is being plundered by a minister and brought to ruin, O Yudhiṣṭhira —
